message.reasoning:
I need to evaluate a trade offer and decide whether to accept, reject, or counter.

I'm checking the color groups to assess the trade. The offer swaps CONNECTICUT_AVENUE for ILLINOIS_AVENUE and SHORT_LINE. I need to verify whether those properties form a complete set.

I have two of three pink properties. Virginia is unowned and would complete the set. p3 owns the other light blue pair, Oriental and Vermont. This makes Connecticut a key blocker.

If I trade Connecticut, p3 would own the full light blue set and could house it heavily. That is a major risk. On the other hand, ILLINOIS_AVENUE would block p2 from completing the red group, which is valuable. p2 currently has only $195 and just one house on dark blues.

SHORT_LINE is a modest addition. The real danger is that p3 already owns both Oriental and Vermont, so completing the light blue set would be catastrophic. I should reject this offer.

Counter offers are not viable. p3 lacks the properties needed to complete my pink set, and I cannot trade Connecticut for cash. Rejecting this offer is the only safe path.

I cannot counter for Virginia Avenue because it is unowned. I need roughly $460 to complete my pink set and buy houses, and I have $476. p3 specifically wants Connecticut to finish the light blue monopoly, so they will not accept a trade for Illinois without that property.

I cannot counter this offer. St. James Place would complete an orange set for p3 or p4. Pennsylvania Avenue would complete a green set for p4. I will reject the trade and keep my pink properties.
